ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
Requirements: To apply to Indiana University, applicants must be on track to earn an accredited high school diploma or equivalent. [1] The application for admission requires an essay. [8] General application requirements include the online application, academic records, and an application fee. [7]
Department: O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs and College of Arts + Sciences
Description: With a major in Environmental Science through a Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science (BSES) degree, you will study the environment and look for solutions to pressing environmental problems. You'll also have opportunities to study abroad in places like South Korea, South Africa, Portugal, and Costa Rica. The BSES is a joint degree program between the O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs and the College of Arts + Sciences—to offer you a selection of courses on a wide range of environmental topics, taught by over 40 faculty and instructors across Indiana University. You'll follow an interdisciplinary approach, gaining knowledge and tools from the traditional sciences, such as biology, chemistry, geology, hydrology, mathematics, meteorology, and physics. [5] Many of the courses include field and laboratory work, providing valuable hands-on experience, and demonstrating the applied nature of environmental science. [5]

[1] With a BAESS, you will gain a broad overview of environmental sustainability problems and the tools needed to address these issues. [1] You'll also have opportunities to explore sustainability globally by studying abroad in places like South Africa, Portugal, or Costa Rica. [1] The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental and Sustainability Studies is an interdisciplinary, liberal-arts degree designed to provide an introduction to the complex system-scale challenges of sustainability as well as the tools needed to address problems that transcend solely social or environmental domains. [4] Students pursuing this degree can expect to integrate experience in the humanities with the natural and social sciences. [1]

Description: Study the complex economic and political factors affecting an issue that is critical to all of us—our health. In the Bachelor of Science in Healthcare Management and Policy program, you'll be taught by nationally known faculty as well as practitioners who understand the issues firsthand: Learn healthcare law from practicing attorneys, long-term care from the administrator of a 300-bed facility, and strategic planning from a hospital CEO. You'll graduate with the leadership skills necessary to ensure people have access to the health services they need—and the analytical skills to reform healthcare from the inside out. [5]

This degree could be a great fit for students who enjoy math, are skilled communicators, and a good at solving problems. With an undergraduate degree from the Kelley School of Business, you'll be able to: analyze and interpret the economic, social, political, legal, cultural, and technological influences that drive the global economy, evaluate a region or nation for business investment or expansion, and develop a comprehensive knowledge base in each essential division of business and understand the important relationships among finance, marketing, operations, and leadership. Minimal chemistry and mathematics requirements allow you to substitute a second major, such as computer science, chemistry, psychology, environmental studies, or business. Because of its flexibility, this degree is ideal for students who wish to pursue a second major, combining the study of biology with another subject area. If you want the flexibility to explore other academic disciplines, wish to teach middle school or high school biology, or desire to work in business, the Biology B.A. degree may be a good option for you. Your work in the major begins with two courses—Foundations of Biology: Diversity, Evolution, and Ecology and Foundations of Biology: Biological Mechanisms. Lab work and courses in molecular biology, genetics, and evolution are also required. Additional lecture courses and lab work enable you to complete the degree. [2]

[11, 13] Following admission to the university and the completion of certain prerequisites, students must then apply for admission to the Teacher Education Program (TEP). The program is designed to equip teacher education candidates with the skills to teach all subjects to children from kindergarten through sixth grade. Students gain a broad background in English, mathematics, humanities, social sciences, and the sciences, which is complemented by classes on teaching methods. A significant part of the curriculum includes multiple field experiences in elementary schools, allowing students to practice and improve their teaching abilities. [1, 4, 9]

[6] Courses in the department emphasize clear and cogent thinking about fundamental problems, locate the origins of these problems in the writings of the great philosophers, and provide in-depth examinations of proposed solutions. [6] The major is flexible enough to meet the needs of those planning to become professional philosophers as well as those with other career goals. [6] Students will develop skills in identifying and critically evaluating arguments, thinking clearly and independently, writing analytically, and applying principles of logic and good reasoning. [7, 9, 10] They will also gain an understanding of the history of Western Philosophy and fundamental issues regarding central philosophical topics, learning to develop and defend their own philosophical views. [7, 9, 10] The program fosters an open-minded, non-dogmatic attitude and the ability to tolerate uncertainty. [7, 10]

Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Physics at Indiana University is a versatile degree preparing students for immediate employment or for advanced studies in physics or related scientific and medical fields. [10] The curriculum covers the foundations of physics, including classical mechanics, classical electrodynamics, quantum mechanics, relativity, and statistical physics, fostering rigorous and analytical thinking. [3] Students are encouraged to participate in research and can choose from programs in optical physics, solid state physics, or biological physics, culminating in a capstone experience in a physics research laboratory. [3] The program is designed to develop problem-solving skills and provides a strong foundation for various careers, including patent law, medicine, and finance, as physicists have been fundamental in inventing technologies like electric motors, lasers, and medical imaging systems. ProgramName: Minor in Native American and Indigenous Studies
Description: The Minor in Native American and Indigenous Studies (NAIS) incorporates perspectives from American Studies, Anthropology, Folklore, History, Literature, Law, Political Science, Visual and Expressive Arts, and other areas of study. Students will learn a broad range of basic historical facts about the Native American and Indigenous peoples of the Americas, to think logically and analytically, to make critical observations, and to formulate interdisciplinary interpretations of the history, literature, art, music, law, politics, and culture of Native American and Indigenous peoples. They will gain new perspectives on globalization, sustainability, and cultural and environmental preservation.

ProgramName: Minor in Philosophy of Mind and Cognition
Description: The minor in Philosophy of Mind and Cognition focuses on foundational questions about the mind and its relation to the rest of nature. You will develop conceptual tools and skills for thinking about the mind from an interdisciplinary standpoint and investigate fundamental questions about the nature of thought, reason, and action. [1] The minor aims to provide familiarity with foundational issues pertaining to the mind as well as with conceptual tools and skills helpful for thinking about the mind from an interdisciplinary standpoint. It will be of interest to students in biology, human biology, psychology, brain science, cognitive science, computer science, informatics, and other areas who are interested in fundamental questions about the nature of the mind, thought, and action. [2]

Description: The Social Justice and Community Engagement Minor is focused on issues of inequality related to race, class, gender, and sexuality. The SJCE Minor is designed to provide students with opportunities to grapple with theory and/or policy issues, to study particular communities and/or social issues, and to integrate work from their previous coursework and apply their knowledge to a specific social justice issue in their community. [1] This program is interdisciplinary, giving you the opportunity to take a rich array of courses spanning the School of Humanities and Social Sciences, and providing a boost to your course of study. After completing your 16 credit hours, you'll engage in a practical, hands-on social justice project in the community. [3]

Description: The mission of the program in Spanish at IU Indianapolis is to assist students in achieving proficiency in the Spanish language and to lead them to an understanding of and appreciation for the wide range of Hispanic cultural, literary, and linguistic manifestations. To meet this goal, the program in Spanish offers introductory and advanced instruction in language, linguistics, culture and civilization, literature, and translation and applied language studies. [9] The introductory and intermediate sequences of courses are designed to provide non-majors with an exploration into Spanish language and Hispanic culture as an essential component of a liberal arts education. [9] The sequences aim to develop an interest in the language and the people who speak it, as well as to prepare students for a variety of careers with international dimensions. [9] The advanced curriculum prepares students to communicate orally and in writing on the different content areas that comprise the study of Spanish, providing them with the knowledge and skills necessary to achieve success in their future careers, to meet their academic and personal goals, and to prepare them for graduate work. [9] Considering the rapidly growing Spanish-speaking population in the United States, Spanish is becoming increasingly desirable in the workplace. [9] The minor in Spanish can be beneficial to students pursuing careers in such fields as education, social services, international business and finance, government service, international communications and information services, and the travel and hospitality industry. [9]
